brief.title: Verify the pinned code in a library checkout
brief.plain_summary: Check the code folder of a fresh library checkout against this pack's pins and run the code's own checks, before any compile or run verb relies on it.
brief.outcome: A verification report: folder digest, module digests, node digests and tests, and each check with its result.

run_tessera_integration.description: Also run the code's Tessera integration check with Tessera at the commit the tool card names.

output_store.description: Store for the produced nouns. The default is a placeholder; use the store your owner assigned.

output_contract.delivery: Write produced nouns surface_only under your own authenticated surface, which is the requester's assigned surface, so the requester and that surface's reviewers can read them. Never use public_commons or allowlist other surfaces. Return every produced noun's pin in output.artifacts; add its value when the requester asks for inline delivery.

outcome_meanings.tools_verified: The declared nouns were produced and every deterministic acceptance check passed.

acceptance_checks.check: The verification report validates against template.verification-report's schema.
code_matches and working_tree_clean are both true.
Every module digest matches the runtime noun.
All 18 node digests and contracts match their node nouns and every built-in test passes.
make check and make demo in the code folder each report pass.

creates.nouns: The worker writes the nouns listed in output_contract.produces and returns their pins.
creates.verbs: The worker proposes follow-up verbs in output.proposed_verbs, such as a breakdown into smaller verbs or a research follow-up, with the pins they need. Proposals are never enqueued by the worker; an authorized requester enqueues the ones worth doing.

required: Verify the pins and check out the library into the task workspace.
Compute the code folder's digest with the tool card's folder rule; require it to equal folder.sha256 and the working tree to be clean, otherwise end blocked.
Install the locked dependencies with uv sync --locked --all-groups in the code folder.
Hash each module the runtime noun lists with its digest rule and compare every digest with its pin.

Load the packaged node catalog in an in-memory database. Compare each node's code_sha256, ports and parameters with its node noun, comparing numbers by value and a parameter marked default_set_in_code by name and type only, then run every node's built-in tests.
Run make check and make demo in the code folder, and record each result with the last lines of its output.

When run_tessera_integration is true, prepare Tessera at the tool card's Tessera commit with uv sync --locked --all-extras and run make tessera-integration in the code folder with TESSERA_DIR set to that checkout.
Return follow-up work the results justify as proposed_verbs and nouns worth creating later as proposed_nouns. Never enqueue them yourself; an authorized requester decides which to run.

an isolated sandbox with git, Python 3.12 or newer and uv, and no credentials
write candidate nouns in the requester's scope
